channel.description: Recent content in Sigil Gate on SigilGate

item.title: 1. Mission and Goals
item.description: Expert voice, audience building, client acquisition, knowledge base

item.title: 2. Target Audience
item.description: Three segments: specialist, user and client, thoughtful reader

item.title: 3. Platforms and Their Strategic Roles
item.description: Six platforms: website, Habr, Zen, Medium, Telegram, Discord

item.title: 4. Content Funnel
item.description: Three funnels: for the specialist, the user, and the thoughtful reader

item.title: 5. Core Content Rubrics
item.description: Two tracks, four rubrics, nine sub-rubrics

item.title: 6. Content Distribution Cycle
item.description: Three loops: continuous, periodic, warm-up

item.title: 7. Metrics
item.description: Measurable indicators by channel: blog, Telegram, Habr, Zen, Medium, GitHub, Discord

item.title: 8. Roadmap
item.description: Three development phases: launch, expansion, growth

item.title: Cryptominer Attack
item.description: How I got hacked, had my CI/CD taken down, and had tokens vacuumed across the entire core cluster — in fifteen minutes.

item.title: A Small Security Fix
item.description: Someone hinted that storing Telegram IDs in plaintext is not a great idea. I fixed it. Here’s how — and why it turned out trickier than expected.

item.title: Terms of Entry
item.description: The project is still closed — but I’ve started bringing in new participants. Here’s how the collaboration works and where it’s all heading.

item.title: I Don't Know How She Does It
item.description: Bot fixed, Habr conquered, personal site under construction, Rustlings resurrected. How do I manage it all? I don’t.

item.title: Too Good an Isolation
item.description: Infrastructure up, bot running — and then it turns out it can’t do anything. The cost of overly tidy containerization.

item.title: Finally Got Around to It
item.description: The Root node has been running for five days. Today I brought up the supporting infrastructure: the admin bot and the subscription microservice — both containerized, with auto-deploy.

item.title: Second-Tier Strategy
item.description: The fire is out — but the aftertaste remains. I reflect on hosting selection criteria: why I avoid European hosting, and why my choice is fourth-tier providers from third-world countries.

item.title: Connection Restored
item.description: Had to unholster the server I’d been keeping in reserve. But the network is up.

item.title: Polite People
item.description: The Japanese support team turned out to be impeccable. The problem, as always, was me.

item.title: All Eggs in One Basket
item.description: A short busy week with no time for the project, support still silent, the network on pause — and some thoughts about eggs, baskets, and diversification.

item.title: Principles of Future Networks
item.description: Five principles for building a detection-resistant network: from protocol selection and client configuration to rotation, layer isolation, and horizontal scaling.

item.title: A Failed Migration
item.description: Unexpected trouble with hosting after migration: servers in Japan suspended without explanation.

item.title: Successfully Completed
item.description: Yesterday I launched the subscription microservice and wrote ‘deployed itself, without a single manual action.’ This morning users couldn’t connect. Not a single one.

item.title: Done Implementing
item.description: Ten days ago I wrote ’the scheme is ready, all that’s left is to implement it.’ Today the subscription microservice is live.

item.title: Connected
item.description: The support system I’d been dreaming of since February is finally built — in a single evening. Tickets, bot-mediated dialogue, handoffs between admins, and broadcasts.

item.title: The Challenge of the Age
item.description: A prophetic article from Habr I couldn’t find again — and the arms race it predicted. From OpenVPN to statistical invisibility.

item.title: 41 Commits
item.description: Today was a cleanup day. No new features, no forward movement on the map. But now several things work the way they were supposed to from the start.

item.title: In the Go Spirit
item.description: A microservice task — and a long-overdue reason to finally try Go in practice. Especially since our project is already soaked in it.

item.title: No Guarantees
item.description: People often ask about the security of our network and what guarantees we offer. Here’s an honest answer — no marketing promises, no fine print.

item.title: Path Rotation: The Client Side
item.description: gRPC path rotation on the Entry→Core segment has been working for a while. Time to close the same gap on the client side — and we finally have a scheme.

item.title: How to Grow a Project Without Accumulating Technical Debt
item.description: “It’s simple and won’t take long” — this is probably the phrase where all technical debt begins. Reflections on two scenarios, invisible work, and a question I don’t have an answer to.

item.title: Economics Over Coffee
item.description: Our financial operator announced an account freeze — so I decided to honestly calculate what the project actually costs. Spoiler: cheaper than it seems.

item.title: Trial Is Live
item.description: The /trial command is up and running: a guest gets a link, a QR code, and an hour of open internet. Here’s how it works under the hood.

item.title: Patterns Kill
item.description: The story of how I lost my VPN in the November wave of blockings — and what it taught me about the nature of DPI: behavioral patterns are more dangerous than any vulnerability in the protocol itself.

item.title: Special
item.description: I never finished most of my projects. But this one won’t end up on the shelf.

item.title: The Telegram Bot
item.description: The project bot gets a new life: from a technical publishing tool to a full-featured interface for network users.

item.title: Picking Up the Pace!
item.description: Automating user and device management, changes to the data storage system, and the idea of trial access via a Telegram bot.

item.title: New Device!
item.description: The ice has broken: an automation scripts repository is up, the architecture is in place, and the first scenario — adding client devices — is already working.

item.title: Data Storage System
item.description: The technical side of the project hasn’t been standing still — I structured the data, chose storage formats, and laid the groundwork for future automation.

item.title: Telegram Blocking
item.description: I barely launched a Telegram channel before they started throttling Telegram. A story about news aging faster than I can write about it.

item.title: Content Strategy
item.description: The taxonomy is a consequence. Behind it lies something more serious: the project’s content strategy.

item.title: Silence Is Deceptive
item.description: No posts doesn’t mean no progress. The project hasn’t gone quiet — quite the opposite. More on that in the upcoming posts.

item.title: KV Stores
item.description: What KV stores are, why they matter for distributed systems, and how etcd became the foundation of operational data storage in Sigil Gate.

item.title: The Data Storage System
item.description: Wanted to create a couple of user accounts — ended up designing a data storage system. A typical weekend.

item.title: When Targeting Hits the Mark
item.description: Searched for a singer named Annette — found the ANet project. Funny how targeted ads work when you’re building a private network.

item.title: The Docs Section
item.description: The project works. The network is up. Now it’s time to bring order to the documentation and make the project truly open.

item.title: The About Section
item.description: The old About page was a placeholder. Now it’s a full section covering goals, mission, team, and an invitation to contribute.

item.title: Systemd timer: time to leave the cave
item.description: I’ve been using cron my whole life. Turns out there’s been something better for quite a while.

item.title: gRPC path rotation
item.description: It’s been on the roadmap for a while — and it’s finally done. The most vulnerable segment of the network is now protected by automatic address rotation.
